literal: To those who wage war even, a fortress is an asset; fearing for oneself, to those who protect even, it is an asset.
translation: A fortress is a valuable asset to those who wage war, and equally an asset to those who fearfully protect themselves.
modern: படையெடுத்துப் போர் செய்பவர்க்கும் அரண் சிறந்த செல்வமாகும்; பகைவர்க்கு அஞ்சித் தம்மைப் பாதுகாத்துக் கொள்பவர்க்கும் அது சிறந்த செல்வமாகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the dual utility of a fortress. For the aggressors (ஆற்றுபவர், here meaning those capable of waging war), a fortress serves as a secure base from which to launch attacks and consolidate power. For the defenders (அஞ்சித் தற்போற்றுபவர்), it provides a safe refuge to protect themselves from enemies. The word பொருள் (wealth/asset) is used twice to emphasize that a fortress is of ultimate value to both the strong who attack and the weak who defend.
